title: I built two in-person retreats. Here's why, and when.
author: Arthur Brooks
summary: Arthur Brooks explains his motivation for creating transformational retreats at Rising Circle Ranch in Santa Fe. He argues that building a more meaningful life requires more than reading alone—it requires time away from routine, a physical space for reflection, and a small group of honest people wrestling with the same existential questions. The article describes two retreats: 'The Meaning of Your Life' (June 14-19) focused on the framework from his book, helping participants clarify why things happen, why they're moving in their current direction, and why their life matters; and 'The Meaning of Us' (June 19-22), an intimate couples retreat co-led by Arthur and his wife Ester designed to help couples fall in love more deeply. The piece emphasizes that transformational work requires active engagement beyond passive reading.
points: Transforming life requires more than reading alone; it needs time away from routine, space for reflection, and a small group wrestling with the same questions. The Meaning of Your Life retreat helps participants clarify their direction by exploring why things happen, why they're moving as they do, and why their life matters. Working through life's big questions with peers who walked those days alongside you creates accountability and insight that solitary reflection cannot provide. Couples who deepen their ability to fall in love more deeply will be better equipped to stay in love for life. Breaking doom loops and identifying which parts of life need nourishing requires structured time and skilled facilitation beyond personal effort.
quotes: Building a more meaningful life requires more than reading alone.
You need a physical space that invites reflection instead of distraction.
You need a small group of honest people wrestling with the same questions you are.
We'll have one big goal: exploring ways to fall in love more deeply, which will help you stay in love for life.
